name: DeepSeek-OCR 2
purpose: Document OCR through visual causal flow: compress the page into few visual tokens, then decode text.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: LICENSE.txt of the official repo is the Apache License 2.0 text (read 2026-11-19); the repo has no LICENSE file by that name, community conversions that say otherwise (DeepSeek license, MIT) do not bind the official weights

architecture.kind: vision-language (deepseek_vl_v2 class), dynamic resolution: up to 6 tiles of 768x768 plus one 1024x1024 view, 144 tokens per tile and 256 global
architecture.why_this_design: Visual causal flow compresses the page into few vision tokens (paper arXiv 2601.20552; claim not re-read).

engine_support.notes: llama.cpp lists DeepSeek-OCR (v1) PR 17400; OCR 2 only via community GGUF

benchmarks.name: MDPBench overall (17 languages)
benchmarks.variant: DeepSeek-OCR (v1, not OCR-2); digital 80.7 vs photographed 42.2

weaknesses: tested only on NVIDIA/CUDA 11.8 setup on the card
third-party MDPBench (v1 model): collapses on photographed pages (42.2) and German (55.0); OCR-2 itself is not in that table
soft.maturity: DeepSeek is a major vendor; the OCR line is a side project

tona_fit.reason: Apache-2.0 verified, but its predecessor is the weakest German/photo result among the tested parsers and it is larger than the 1B parsers that score higher; its vision-token compression stays interesting.

open_questions: German and photographed-page accuracy of OCR-2 (MDPBench measured only v1)

sources.note: MDPBench README table read directly; an earlier summarizer pass mislabeled the Latin-average column as DE, the DE values here come from the dataset README

pc-16gb.notes: BF16 about 2 GB; Tona runs one model at a time, so it replaces the resident model while it works
